name: temporal-tag-error-delay-not-convertible
description: In a timeline table (a table with an onset column), a Delay tag has a value that cannot be converted to the default units of its unit class because the unit has no conversionFactor (month and year in HED 8.4.0), so the delayed onset cannot be placed on the timeline. Delay is never allowed in a descriptor table (cause k), so it can never carry a non-convertible unit. Appendix B TEMPORAL_TAG_ERROR cause n. Implemented in hed-python PR #1399; hed-javascript issue #860.
common_causes: Using a calendar unit such as month or year for a Delay
Assuming every unit in a unit class converts to the default unit
Not noticing that a unit lacks a conversionFactor in the schema
explanation: In a timeline table a Delay is added to the row's onset to place its inner group on the table's timeline. That is only possible when the value can be converted to the default unit of the unit class (seconds for timeUnits). A unit with no conversionFactor, such as month or year, has no conversion, so the delayed onset cannot be computed and the annotation is an error.
correction_strategy: Express the Delay in a unit that has a conversionFactor (s, ms, minute, hour, day)

correction_examples.explanation: Replaced month, which has no conversionFactor, with day, which converts to seconds
Replaced year with an equivalent count of days

correction_patterns: Use only units with a conversionFactor in Delay values
Check the schema unit class listing when an unusual unit is needed
Prefer s or ms for delays in event files
fix_instructions: 1. Find the Delay tag reported on the row
2. Look up its unit in the schema and confirm it has no conversionFactor
3. Rewrite the value in a unit that has one (s, ms, minute, hour, day)
4. Revalidate the events file
validation_hints: Only applies to timeline tables (with an onset column), where the delayed onset is computed; Delay is banned outright from descriptor tables
Report on the row that holds the Delay; validate the rest of the file normally
The unit itself is valid, so UNITS_INVALID is not the right code
specification_reference: Appendix B, TEMPORAL_TAG_ERROR cause n; 3.2.8.4 Duration and Delay

name: temporal-tag-error-duration-not-convertible
description: In a timeline table (a table with an onset column), a Duration tag has a value that cannot be converted to the default units of its unit class because the unit has no conversionFactor (month and year in HED 8.4.0), so the end time cannot be placed on the timeline. The same Duration is valid in a descriptor table such as participants.tsv, where there is no timeline to map it onto. Appendix B TEMPORAL_TAG_ERROR cause n.
common_causes: Using a calendar unit such as month or year for a Duration in an events file
Assuming every unit in a unit class converts to the default unit
Copying a Duration that is fine in participants.tsv into a timeline table
explanation: In a timeline table a Duration is added to the row's onset to give the end time of its group on the table's timeline. That is only possible when the value can be converted to the default unit of the unit class (seconds for timeUnits). A unit with no conversionFactor, such as month or year, has no conversion, so the end time cannot be computed and the annotation is an error. In a descriptor table nothing is placed on a timeline, so Duration may use any valid unit of its unit class there.
correction_strategy: In a timeline table, express the Duration in a unit that has a conversionFactor (s, ms, minute, hour, day); leave a Duration in a descriptor table as it is

correction_examples.explanation: In an events file, replaced year, which has no conversionFactor, with an equivalent count of days
The Delay was already convertible; the paired Duration must be too

correction_patterns: Use only units with a conversionFactor in Duration values in timeline tables
Check the schema unit class listing when an unusual unit is needed
Prefer s or ms for durations in event files
fix_instructions: 1. Confirm the file has an onset column; if not, the Duration is valid and nothing needs to change
2. Find the Duration tag reported on the row
3. Look up its unit in the schema and confirm it has no conversionFactor
4. Rewrite the value in a unit that has one (s, ms, minute, hour, day)
5. Revalidate the events file
validation_hints: Only applies to timeline tables (with an onset column), where the end time is computed
A Duration with any valid unit passes in a file without an onset column
Report on the row that holds the Duration; validate the rest of the file normally
The unit itself is valid, so UNITS_INVALID is not the right code
A group pairing a convertible Delay with a non-convertible Duration is still an error
specification_reference: Appendix B, TEMPORAL_TAG_ERROR cause n; 3.2.8.4 Duration and Delay

name: temporal-tag-error-delay-with-anchored-marker
description: A `Delay` tag may appear in an `Onset`, `Offset`, or `Inset` group, delaying that marker; the marker tag must stay at the top level of the group, not inside the delayed inner group.
common_causes: Nesting the Onset, Offset, or Inset inside the Delay's inner group
Assuming Delay may only be paired with Duration
explanation: A Delay in an Onset, Offset, or Inset group places that marker at the row's onset plus the delay. The Delay, the anchor, and the marker tag are all top-level members of the same group; wrapping the anchor and marker in an inner group nests a top-level tag and is an error.
correction_strategy: Keep Delay, the Def anchor, and the Onset/Offset/Inset tag together at the top level of one group

correction_examples.explanation: The Onset and its anchor belong beside the Delay, not in an inner group
The Inset and its anchor belong beside the Delay, not in an inner group

correction_patterns: Unwrap (Def/x, Onset) when it sits inside a Delay group
Put Delay in the same group as the anchored marker
fix_instructions: 1. Find Delay groups whose inner group contains Onset, Offset, or Inset
2. Move the anchor and the marker tag up beside the Delay
3. Keep at most one additional inner tag group for an Onset or Inset, and none for an Offset
validation_hints: Delay may accompany Duration, Onset, Offset, or Inset in one top-level group
A temporal tag inside a nested group is always an error
specification_reference: 3.2.8.3. Onset, Offset, and Inset; 3.2.8.4. Duration and Delay

name: temporal-tag-error-duration-with-top-level-def
description: A Duration group may not have a Def tag or a Def-expand group at its top level (rule 2: Duration has no anchor); one may appear inside the inner group. A Def-expand group stands where its Def tag would and is never counted as the inner group.
common_causes: Writing a Duration group like an Onset group, with the definition as an anchor beside it
Counting a Def-expand group as the Duration's inner group
explanation: Onset, Offset, and Inset groups are anchored by a Def tag or Def-expand group that names the ongoing event. A Duration group has no anchor: everything it describes goes in its one inner group, and that includes a Def tag. A Def-expand group is the expanded form of a Def tag, so the same rule applies to it, and it does not count as the inner group.
correction_strategy: Move the Def tag or Def-expand group into the Duration's inner group

correction_examples.explanation: The Def tag is the inner group
The Def tag joins the inner group
The Def-expand group goes inside the inner group

specification_reference: 3.2.8. Reserved tags (rule 2, table column Anchor); 3.2.8.2. Def and Def-expand tags; Appendix B TEMPORAL_TAG_ERROR l

name: temporal-tag-error-rules-apply-in-8-1-0
description: The reserved-tag rules for Delay and Duration apply in every standard schema version, including 8.1.0, whose schema gives these tags none of the reserved, topLevelTagGroup, or requireChild attributes: a nested or ungrouped Delay or Duration, one without a value, and a Delay in a descriptor table all fail; (Delay/2 s, (Blue)) and (Onset, Def/MyColor, Delay/3 s) in a timeline table pass.
common_causes: Reading the 8.0.0 or 8.1.0 schema, which does not mark Delay and Duration as reserved or top-level, and treating them as ordinary tags
Leaving out the time value because the 8.1.0 schema does not mark Delay and Duration requireChild
Putting a Delay in a table without an onset column
explanation: Delay and Duration follow the same rules in every standard schema version: each must head its own top-level group, take a time value, and (when it is the only reserved tag of its group) have exactly one inner group, and Delay may appear only in a timeline table. The 8.0.0 and 8.1.0 schemas do not carry the attributes that state these rules; the reserved-tag rules of the specification supply them, so annotations validated against those schemas are checked the same way as under later ones.
correction_strategy: Put each Delay or Duration, with a time value, at the top level of its own group with one inner group describing the event, and use Delay only in tables with an onset column

correction_examples.explanation: Duration heads a top-level group with one inner group
The Duration group moves to the top level
Duration needs a time value

specification_reference: 3.2.8. Reserved tags (table rows Delay and Duration; rules 1, 3 and 4); Appendix B TEMPORAL_TAG_ERROR a, b, k; Appendix B TAG_REQUIRES_CHILD b

name: temporal-tag-error-no-conversion-factor-in-8-0-0
description: Standard schema 8.0.0 gives no time unit a conversionFactor. In a timeline table a Delay or Duration value in the default unit, given or omitted and written as s, second, or seconds, is taken as is, so (Duration/3 s, (Red)), (Duration/3, (Red)) and (Duration/3 second, (Red)) pass; a modified form or any other unit cannot be placed on the timeline, so (Duration/300 ms, (Red)) and (Duration/2 minute, (Red)) fail (cause n). The same Duration passes in a descriptor table.
common_causes: Using minute, hour, or day for a Delay or Duration in an events file validated against 8.0.0
Assuming the conversion factors of later schemas are available in 8.0.0
explanation: In a timeline table a Delay or Duration is placed on the table's timeline, which needs the value in seconds. Standard schema 8.0.0 gives none of its time units a conversionFactor, so only a value already in the default unit (s, second, or seconds, or no unit, which means s) can be placed; a value in milliseconds, minutes, hours, or days cannot. In a descriptor table nothing is placed on a timeline, so a Duration may use any valid time unit there.
correction_strategy: Under 8.0.0, write Delay and Duration values in a timeline table in seconds, or validate against a later schema version, whose time units have conversion factors

correction_examples.explanation: Under 8.0.0 only seconds can be placed on the timeline
Later schemas give minute a conversionFactor

specification_reference: 3.2.8.4 Duration and Delay; Appendix B TEMPORAL_TAG_ERROR n
